pk.context: 5 mg subcutaneous, single dose, healthy adults

pill.desc: clear, colorless to slightly yellow solution in a prefilled single-dose pen

tell: A dual GIP and GLP-1 receptor agonist whose C20 fatty diacid binds albumin to prolong its action.

clues.text: Mean absolute bioavailability after subcutaneous injection is 80%. It is 99% bound to plasma albumin, and the drug is cleared mainly as metabolites in urine and feces.
Carries aminoisobutyric acid at positions 2 and 13 and a C-terminal amide, with a molecular weight of 4813.53 Da. It is supplied as a sterile solution.
Approved under an NDA in single-dose pens and vials and multi-dose pens and vials, in strengths from 2.5 mg to 15 mg. Dosed once weekly.

Boxed warning for thyroid C-cell tumors. Contraindicated with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN 2, and with serious hypersensitivity; decreased appetite and constipation are common.
Adjunct to diet and exercise for glycemic control in adults and children aged 10 and over with type 2 diabetes, and to lower major cardiovascular events in adults at high risk.

Selectively binds and activates both GIP and GLP-1 receptors, the targets of the native hormones. It enhances first- and second-phase insulin secretion and lowers glucagon, all in a glucose-dependent manner.
The generic name begins with T and has eleven letters.
